venue: Chase Field (Phoenix, AZ, 401 East Jefferson Street). CONFIRMED CURRENT for the 2026 season, 16 August 2026. (1) RateYourSeats event listings fetched on 16 Aug 2026 show every 2026 Diamondbacks home game at 'Chase Field - Phoenix, AZ' (e.g. 'Aug 21 Fri 6:40pm Cincinnati Reds at Arizona Diamondbacks Chase Field - Phoenix, AZ', 'Sep 20 Sun 1:10pm New York Yankees at Arizona Diamondbacks Chase Field - Phoenix, AZ') - https://www.rateyourseats.com/chase-field/seating/field-seats . (2) Ballparks of Baseball (page copy updated for 2026: 'Prior to the start of the 2026 season, the Diamondbacks added a new 9,600 square foot scoreboard, 52% larger than the previous one in centerfield.') lists the venue as CHASE FIELD and states verbatim: '-Naming Rights: Chase, $2.2 million/year through 2028' and '-Former Name(s): Bank One Ballpark' - https://www.ballparksofbaseball.com/ballparks/chase-field/ . (3) Wikipedia: 'Chase Field, formerly Bank One Ballpark, is a retractable roof stadium in downtown Phoenix, Arizona... It is the ballpark of Major League Baseball's Arizona Diamondbacks.' and 'Former names: Bank One Ballpark (1998-2005)'; official website field 'mlb.com/dbacks/ballpark' - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chase_Field . (4) Itinerant Fan stadium guide, 'Most recent update: March 27, 2026', still titled 'Chase Field' and lists capacity 48,330 - https://itinerantfan.com/stadium-guide/chase-field/ . (5) Shaded Seats page modified 2026-03-24 still 'Shaded Seats at Chase Field' - https://www.shadedseats.com/chase-field-shaded-seats/ . RENAME RISK CHECKED AND NOT FOUND: the naming-rights deal runs through 2028, so no rename has occurred or been announced for 2026. NEWS CONTEXT (relevant but NOT a rename): Wikipedia states 'In September 2025, Arizona House Bill 2704 was formally signed into law which would allow sales tax dollars to fund renovations of the stadium'; Itinerant Fan adds 'major changes could be coming soon after the state of Arizona approved funding for renovations to the nearly 30-year-old facility' (linking an ESPN story headlined 'Diamondbacks remain [at] Chase Field [for] 30 years [after] approval [of] renovation bill'). So the team is STAYING at Chase Field, under that name, with a renovation programme ahead. The RateYourSeats internal master_id is 'chase-field-phoenix-az' and the slug is 'chase-field'.
concert_only_sections: NOTE: these nine entries appear in the RateYourSeats venue section index labelled 'Field 1' ... 'Field 9' but with URLs https://www.rateyourseats.com/chase-field/seating/sections/1 ... /sections/9 . They are the concert floor sections laid on the playing surface and MUST NOT be treated as baseball sections; a bare '1'..'9' in ticket data would collide with nothing at Chase Field (there are no numeric single-digit baseball sections) but the display label is 'Field N'. The RYS concert zone page states verbatim: 'For concerts, the field is reconfigured with a large stage typically placed in the outfield, and field seating sections are arranged across the playing surface.' and 'Many events also include a General Admission (GA) section near the front of the stage for fans who want to stand and enjoy the concert in an open, interactive setting.' - https://www.rateyourseats.com/chase-field/seating/field-seats

NOTE: the index also carries two zone links that are not individual sections and are excluded from 'sections': 'Left Field Terrace' -> /chase-field/seating/cold-beer-cheeseburgers-terrace (a baseball area, but RYS gives it no numbered section IDs; its rows are labelled 'T' for table seating) and 'Field Sections' -> /chase-field/seating/field-seats (concert only).

Reason: two independent 2026-current sources give 48,330, and Wikipedia's own capacity history identifies 48,633 as the 2011-2014 figure, so Ballparks of Baseball is simply stale. orientation.batter_faces: Approximately NORTH (some sources say north-northeast). Center field points north; the batter at home plate faces north. Right field is on the EAST side of the park, left field on the WEST side. Consequently the first-base / right-field stands face roughly west-northwest and take the afternoon sun, while the third-base / left-field stands are the shade side in the afternoon and evening.
orientation.confidence: medium - two sources agree on 'north' / 'northeast', and the compass claim is independently corroborated by the sun-path description and by the official D-backs gate geometry (Gate K, at the ballpark's northeast corner, is the gate nearest Section 105 in right field). But no source gives a precise bearing in degrees, and 'north' vs 'northeast' are not reconciled. Note that at Chase Field orientation is largely moot in practice because the roof is usually closed.
orientation.source: https://www.shadedseats.com/chase-field-shaded-seats/ - verbatim: 'Chase Field is oriented to the north. Each morning the sun rises over the right field corner, swings around home plate at mid-day and sets behind the left field wall. When the roof is open, this configuration makes the 3rd base side of the park the "shade side," while the 1st base side and right field are the sunny spots.' and 'The right field corner, sections 101-110, is particularly exposed, and those sensitive to the sun should avoid it.' SECOND SOURCE (web search summary of intheballparks.com / charliesballparks.com): 'For the rare occasions when the roof is open, usually for cooler evening games in April or late September, the stadium faces northeast.' INDEPENDENT GEOMETRIC CROSS-CHECK (official Diamondbacks ADA page): 'The designated drop-off point for all guests is located on the south side of Jefferson Street, just west of 7th Street. This is at the northeast corner of Chase Field near Gate K.' combined with 'Elevator Locations: Across from Sections 105 / 200 / 300 - closest to Gate K' - i.e. the NORTHEAST corner of the building is where Section 105 (right field) sits, which is exactly what a north-facing centre field requires. https://www.mlb.com/dbacks/ballpark/information/ada . ROOF: Wikipedia - 'Chase Field was the first stadium built in the United States with a retractable roof over a natural grass playing surface, although it has used artificial turf since 2019.' and 'Following the introduction of a synthetic playing surface, the roof is kept mostly closed and is opened only on game days when weather permits.'

numbering_direction.summary: Section numbers INCREASE FROM THE RIGHT-FIELD / FIRST-BASE SIDE TOWARD THE LEFT-FIELD / THIRD-BASE SIDE on EVERY level, and the lettered field-level sections do the same (A at the first-base end, S at the third-base end). On a standard chart drawn with home plate at the bottom, the numbers run CLOCKWISE. The bowl is a horseshoe broken at dead centre field by the 25-foot batter's-eye wall, so the low end and the high end of each series are the two outfield ends, not adjacent. Concretely: 100 LEVEL - 101-105 are the RIGHT FIELD bleachers (101 in right-CENTER next to the batter's eye and the pool, 105 at the right-field end next to the visiting bullpen), 106-110 finish the right-field corner, roughly 111-117 run down the FIRST BASE line, ~118-127 wrap BEHIND HOME PLATE (122 is the flagged home-plate section; the netting range 115-129 and the elevators at 117 and 127 bracket it symmetrically), ~128-135 run down the THIRD BASE line, 136-138 are the LEFT FIELD corner at the foul pole, and 139-144 are the LEFT FIELD bleachers (139 next to the Diamondbacks bullpen, 144 in left-CENTER next to the batter's eye). 200 LEVEL (Club / Diamond Level) - 200 at the right-field end, 200-209 down the first base side, 210A-210I directly BEHIND HOME PLATE, 211-220 down the third base side, 221-223 in the LEFT FIELD corner. 300 LEVEL (upper deck) - 300 at the right-field end, 301-315 down the first base side, ~314-318 BEHIND HOME PLATE with 316 the flagged home-plate section, 317-327 down the third base side, 328-332 the LEFT FIELD corner. FIELD LEVEL LETTERS - A and B (1st Base Box) then C-F (Dugout Box, visiting dugout) on the FIRST BASE side, G-M (Clubhouse Box / Home Plate Box) BEHIND HOME PLATE, N-Q (Dugout Box, Diamondbacks dugout) then R and S (3rd Base Box) on the THIRD BASE side. Every level therefore runs the same way and the levels align vertically: the official D-backs elevator list pairs 105/200/300, 117/209/310, 127/211/321 and 139/223/332.

anchors.where: RIGHT FIELD (anchor #1, the required right-field anchor). Verbatim: 'Home Run Territory: Sections 101-105 (right field) and 139-144 (left field) behind the outfield walls' and 'Bleacher seating at Chase Field is located behind the outfield walls in two main areas: Right Field: Sections 101-105 / Left Field: Sections 139-144'. Also 'Sections in right-center field (Section 101) are among the best in this area, offering slightly better angles toward home plate and proximity to key attractions.' - so 101 is the right-CENTER end (next to the batter's eye) and 105 is the far end of the right-field group.
RIGHT FIELD CORNER, independent of RateYourSeats. Verbatim: 'The right field corner, sections 101-110, is particularly exposed, and those sensitive to the sun should avoid it.'

RIGHT FIELD - visiting bullpen. Verbatim: 'Fans looking to be near the action can sit: Near the visiting bullpen (Section 105) / Near the Diamondbacks bullpen (Section 139)'. Independently corroborated by web search of aviewfrommyseat.com and Clem's Baseball: 'Diamondbacks Bullpen: The Diamondbacks bullpen is located in left field near Section 139. Visitors Bullpen: The visiting team's bullpen is located in right field near Section 105.' Further corroborated by the official D-backs ADA page: 'All public pay phones are fully accessible with at least one public pay phone featuring a TDD/TTY near the First Aid Station behind Section 105.'

BEHIND HOME PLATE - 100 level (anchor #2, the required home-plate anchor). Section Insights list 'Home Plate View' and the Seating Notes say verbatim: 'For baseball games, desirable view from behind home plate'. Corroborated by the netting range on the same page: 'Front of sections 115-129 are behind the netting - There is some amount of netting or screening in front of sections 115-129.' 122 is the exact arithmetic centre of 115-129.

LEFT FIELD (anchor #3, the required left-field anchor). Verbatim: 'Left Field: Sections 139-144' and 'Near the Diamondbacks bullpen (Section 139)'. Section 144's own page carries a fan review from Row 11: 'The seat we had were pretty good. we were right in the first row in the outfield along the yellow hr line.'

LEFT FIELD CORNER at the foul pole - high numbers. Verbatim: 'In the left field corner, Sections 136-138 offer an interesting option as you can find some more affordable lower level seats. However the foul pole can cause some viewing obstructions in many of the areas, so we recommend staying in the lower numbered seats of Section 136 or the higher numbered seats of Section 138 where the sight lines are more clear.'
FIRST BASE LINE - low-middle numbers. Verbatim: 'For the best overall experience from the lower endzone options, we recommend the higher rows of Sections 114-117 (along the first base line).'
anchors.source: https://www.rateyourseats.com/chase-field/seating/sections/144 and /sections/143 (RYS '100 Level Endzone (Football)' expert review block)

anchors.where: THIRD BASE LINE - high-middle numbers. The '100 Level Sideline (Football)' review served on Section 128's page says verbatim: 'Most 100 level sections along the third base line end at Row 40, making seats in Rows 30 and higher an excellent choice.' Section 128 is indeed labelled 'Rows 21-39, 40C-40W'.

anchors.section: A, B (first base) vs R, S (third base)
anchors.where: FIELD LEVEL LETTERS increase from first base toward third base. Verbatim: 'Premium Infield Seating: Sections A-B (1st base side) and R-S (3rd base side) just beyond the dugouts' and '1st Base Box: Sections A and B (first base side) / 3rd Base Box: Sections R and S (third base side)'.

FIELD LEVEL LETTERS, dugout blocks. Verbatim: 'Dugout Box seating is located in sections C-F (first base side) and N-Q (third base side), directly behind the team dugouts on the lower level.' and 'Directly Behind Dugouts: Sections C-F (visitors) and N-Q (Diamondbacks) on the lower level'. Corroborated independently: 'Lettered sections A-F on the first base side are also known as the Dugout Box.'

BEHIND HOME PLATE - field level. Verbatim: 'Home Plate Premium Seats: Sections G-M (Rows A-F) located directly between the dugouts at field level' and 'Clubhouse Box seating is located directly behind home plate between the dugouts, spanning sections G-M in the front rows of the ballpark.' and 'Home Plate Box seating is located in the back half of sections G-M, directly behind home plate.'

BEHIND HOME PLATE - 200 (Club / Diamond) level. Verbatim: 'The most desirable seats on this level are the 210-level sections labeled 210A-210I, which sit directly behind home plate and provide the best combination of view and location.' and 'Sections behind home plate (210A-210I) provide the most centered perspective, while seats farther down the baselines still offer strong angles with full-field visibility.' Section 210E's own page shows Section Insights 'Home Plate View' and Seating Notes 'For baseball games, desirable view from behind home plate'.

LEFT FIELD CORNER - 200 level, high numbers. Verbatim: 'These seats are located in sections 221-223 on the 200 level, positioned down the left field line in the corner.' and 'The height allows fans to see the full field, but the left field corner angle makes it harder to follow action at home plate.' Corroborated: 'some obstructions will be found in Sections 221-223 due to the left field foul pole.'

BEHIND HOME PLATE - 300 (upper) level. Section Insights list 'Home Plate View' and Seating Notes say verbatim: 'For baseball games, desirable view from behind home plate'. Zone context: 'MVP Box seating is located in sections 310-322, positioned along the infield on the upper level.'

300 level: home plate is the mid-310s, the LEFT FIELD corner is the high 320s/330s. Verbatim: 'Seats deep in the left field corner and directly behind home plate are under the structures that attach to the retractable roof. Sections 314-318 and 328-332 are the safest options, while rows toward the back of sections 319-327 should also get roof protection from the sun.'

OFFICIAL DIAMONDBACKS ELEVATOR LIST - the single strongest independent cross-check, because elevator banks are physically stacked and roughly symmetric about home plate. Verbatim: 'Elevator Locations: Across from Sections 105 / 200 / 300 - closest to Gate K; Across from Sections 117 / 209 / 310 - closest to Gate J (priority given to our guests with disabilities); Across from Sections 127 / 211 / 321 - closest to Gate E (priority given to our guests with disabilities); Across from Sections 139 / 223 / 332 - closest to Gate A.' This proves (a) 105, 200 and 300 are the same physical corner (right field, and Gate K is stated elsewhere on the same page to be at the ballpark's NORTHEAST corner), (b) 139, 223 and 332 are the same physical corner (left field), and (c) the two infield banks at 117/209/310 and 127/211/321 bracket home plate symmetrically - giving ~122 on the 100 level, ~210 on the 200 level and ~315/316 on the 300 level as the centre, exactly matching the RateYourSeats home-plate anchors.

GUEST RELATIONS desks - a second official symmetric landmark, sited just off home plate on the main and upper concourses. Verbatim: 'During every event, Guest Relations' desks are located on the main concourse across from Section 128 and on the upper concourse across from Section 322.' and 'If you need a large print map or D-backs schedule, go to Guest Relations near Section 128 or 322.'

numbering_direction.confidence: high - five independent RateYourSeats zone pages, four RateYourSeats section pages, the official Diamondbacks ADA elevator/gate list, ShadedSeats' sun-and-corner description, and the bullpen locations all agree, and the official elevator list independently ties 105/200/300 together at one outfield corner and 139/223/332 together at the other. No source anywhere contradicts 'low numbers = right field / first base, high numbers = left field / third base'.

home_plate_sections._notes: EVERY tier at Chase Field wraps behind home plate - none needs a 'NONE' entry. FIELD LEVEL: fully sourced - 'Sections G-M (Rows A-F) located directly between the dugouts at field level' (Clubhouse Box) and 'Home Plate Box seating is located in the back half of sections G-M, directly behind home plate.' No source names a single centre letter; J is the arithmetic centre of G-M but that is an INFERENCE. 100 LEVEL: only Section 122 is explicitly flagged by RateYourSeats as a home-plate section ('Home Plate View' insight plus 'For baseball games, desirable view from behind home plate'). The behind-the-plate BLOCK is wider - the netting runs 115-129 and the flanking elevators sit at 117 and 127 - so 118-127 is the practical behind-the-plate arc, but 121 and 123 are NOT individually sourced. 200 LEVEL: fully sourced, the whole 210A-210I block is stated to 'sit directly behind home plate'; 210E is the middle letter and its own page carries the 'Home Plate View' insight, so 210E is the best single centre. 300 LEVEL: only Section 316 is explicitly flagged ('Home Plate View' + 'desirable view from behind home plate'); ShadedSeats' 'directly behind home plate' band is 314-318, and the flanking elevators are at 310 and 321, so 315/316 is the centre. 315 is NOT individually sourced.

levels.name: Field Level - lettered sections (Clubhouse Box, Home Plate Box, Dugout Box, 1st/3rd Base Boxes)
levels.sections: A, AW, B, BW, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, J, K, L, M, N, O, P, Q, R, RFW, S
levels.notes: The innermost, closest-to-the-field ring, in front of the 100 Level bowl. Runs A/B (1st Base Box, first base side) -> C-F (Dugout Box, in front of the VISITING dugout) -> G-M (Clubhouse Box in the front rows, Home Plate Box in the back half, directly behind home plate) -> N-Q (Dugout Box, in front of the DIAMONDBACKS dugout) -> R/S (3rd Base Box, third base side). Verbatim from the zone pages: 'Premium Infield Seating: Sections A-B (1st base side) and R-S (3rd base side) just beyond the dugouts'; 'Close-to-Field Views: Only 7 rows per section with excellent proximity to infield action'; 'Each section includes just 7 rows, keeping fans close to the field and creating a more exclusive, low-density seating area.'; 'Directly Behind Dugouts: Sections C-F (visitors) and N-Q (Diamondbacks) on the lower level'; 'Close-to-Field Experience: Rows 6-18 with Row 6 closest to the dugout'; 'Rows in these sections run from Row 6 to Row 18, with Row 6 closest to the dugout. Because the dugouts sit below field level, these seats are slightly elevated above the players'; 'Home Plate Premium Seats: Sections G-M (Rows A-F) located directly between the dugouts at field level'; 'These seats are limited to Rows A-F, placing fans extremely close to the field'; 'Home Plate Box seating is located in the back half of sections G-M, directly behind the Clubhouse Box seats'. RateYourSeats also notes for football: 'Lettered sections A-F on the first base side are also known as the Dugout Box, where fans will find more spacious legroom and closer proximity to the field, but will have a very shallow seating height' and 'Lettered sections behind home plate are also known as the Club House Box, which will have roomier, more comfortable seating, but a poor viewing height for seeing all areas of the field.' AW, BW and RFW are wheelchair-suffixed variants of A, B and (presumably) a Right Field section; RYS has no photo or row data for any of them. Club access for A/B/G-M/R/S: 'Access to the Sedona Club', 'Access to the Sonoran Room', 'Access to the BMW Homeplate Lounge'.

levels.name: 100 Level (main lower bowl, including the outfield bleachers)
levels.notes: 101-105 right field bleachers, 106-110 right field corner, ~111-117 first base line, ~118-127 behind home plate, ~128-135 third base line, 136-138 left field corner at the foul pole, 139-144 left field bleachers. Infield sections are labelled 'Rows 21-39, 40C-40W' (e.g. 122, 128) - i.e. the 100 Level infield STARTS at Row 21, because Rows 1-20 belong to the lettered Field Level in front of it. Verbatim: '100 Level Infield seating provides fans with close views of the field from 1st base to 3rd base inside the inner seating bowl. Located just behind the Field Level sections, none of the 100 Level Infield sections extend to the field... The seating sections start at row 21 in the front and run through row 39 in the back. These seats are in a good area to catch a foul ball, and with the retractable roof (and stadium air conditioning), fans should have little concern about the sun.' Bleachers verbatim: 'Classic Bleacher Seating: Long bench-style rows with up to ~40 rows per section'; 'These sections feature bench-style bleacher seating with long rows and a more traditional ballpark feel. Some sections can have up to 40 rows, making them larger than many other areas of the stadium.'; 'Sun Exposure: Right field bleachers get the most sun when the roof is open'. Observed row labels: 101 = 'Rows 22-31'; 143 and 144 = 'Rows 11-39, 40C-40W'; 122 and 128 = 'Rows 21-39, 40C-40W'; 100W = 'Rows 1C-1W'. Ballparks of Baseball describes the bowl verbatim: 'The seating arrangement features a four-tier grandstand that stretches from the left-field foul pole to home plate and around to the right-field foul pole. Bleacher seats are situated behind both the left and right-field fences, while a 25-foot center-field wall serves as the hitter's backdrop, with the main video scoreboard positioned above it.'

levels.name: 200 Level - Club Level (also called the Diamond Level)
levels.notes: Verbatim: 'Upgraded 200 Level Seating: Sections 200-220 wrap around the infield at an ideal mid-level height for balanced, full-field views'; 'The Club Level (also known as the Diamond Level) includes sections 200-220, wrapping around the infield at an ideal height for viewing the game.'; 'This level is divided into three seating styles: Club Terrace / Club Box / Club Reserve'; 'Smaller, Less Crowded Sections: Most sections have fewer than 12 rows and ~20 seats per row, leading to shorter lines and easier movement'; 'The most desirable seats on this level are the 210-level sections labeled 210A-210I, which sit directly behind home plate'. The 210A-210I sections are tiny: 'Behind home plate, fans will find the clearest views among the Club Corner options and will also have some of the smallest seating sections in the entire park (no more than 2 rows of seating in each).' Section 210E is labelled 'Rows 1C, 1, 1W'. Sections 221-223 sit past the stated 200-220 club range, in the left field corner, and hold the All-You-Can-Eat seats: 'These seats are located in sections 221-223 on the 200 level, positioned down the left field line in the corner.' Section 216 is used as the Club Level hero photo ('Section 216, Row 10'), and 221 as the All-You-Can-Eat hero ('Section 221, Row 10'). Amenities: 'Access to the BMW Club Bar', in-seat service, private restrooms. RYS has NO row data or photo for 214L, 215L or 224W.

levels.name: 300 Level - Upper Deck (Infield Reserved / MVP Box front rows)
levels.notes: Verbatim: 'The 300 Level is the highest seating area at Chase Field, offering less desirable views of the field than most other areas at the ballpark. From the Infield portion of the 300 Level (also known as Infield Reserved), fans will have good sight lines to the center field scoreboard, and while the play on the field might be far, you're sure to save a few dollars on the cost of your ticket. Sections here are among some of the largest with up to 40 rows of seating per section. Entry tunnels are located near the bottom of the sections (at Row 4), so fans who don't want a long walk to the restrooms and concessions should avoid seats in the higher rows.' Corner variant: 'Sections here have up to 32 numbered rows of seating, and entry tunnels located near the front at Row 4. If possible we recommend staying in Rows 1-5 to avoid feeling too far from the action.' MVP Box (front rows only): 'Best Upper Level Seats: Located in the front rows (1-7) of sections 310-322 along the infield'; 'These seats are specifically found in the first seven rows of each section'; 'Convenient Access: Entry tunnel at Row 4 allows quick access to concourse and amenities'. Observed row label for Section 316: 'Rows 1-3, 4C-4W, 8-32' with 'There is wheelchair seating betweeen Rows 4W and 8' [sic, RYS typo]. Wikipedia adds: 'With 80% of the seats in foul territory, the upper deck is one of the highest in the majors. The park's suites are tucked far under the third deck, which keeps the upper deck closer to the action, with the exception of the Dugout Suites which sit next to the home and visitor's dugouts.' Itinerant Fan adds: 'Chase Field's lower and upper seating tiers seem to have endless numbers of rows - this is important to know if you have tickets high in the upper deck, as you'll have to be prepared for quite a bit of stair-walking to get to your seats.'

dugouts.home: THIRD BASE side. The Diamondbacks (home) dugout is on the third base side, in front of field-level lettered Sections N-Q. NOTE: this is the LESS common arrangement in MLB and is easy to get backwards - it has been verified against two independent sources.
dugouts.visiting: FIRST BASE side, in front of field-level lettered Sections C-F.
dugouts.source: https://www.rateyourseats.com/chase-field/seating/dugout-box - verbatim: 'Directly Behind Dugouts: Sections C-F (visitors) and N-Q (Diamondbacks) on the lower level' and 'Dugout Box seating is located in sections C-F (first base side) and N-Q (third base side), directly behind the team dugouts on the lower level.' and 'For team-specific seating: Diamondbacks dugout: Sections N-Q (third base side) / Visiting team dugout: Sections C-F (first base side)'. INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION (non-RateYourSeats): https://www.ballparksofbaseball.com/ballparks/chase-field/ states verbatim in its Facts & Figures block: '-Home Dugout: Third Base'. These two agree, so the third-base home dugout is treated as CONFIRMED. Rows behind the dugouts run 6-18, Row 6 closest.

bullpens: Both bullpens are beyond the outfield fences, at the bases of the two bleacher groups - the VISITING bullpen in RIGHT field and the DIAMONDBACKS bullpen in LEFT field. RateYourSeats verbatim: 'Fans looking to be near the action can sit: Near the visiting bullpen (Section 105) / Near the Diamondbacks bullpen (Section 139)' - https://www.rateyourseats.com/chase-field/seating/bleacher-seats . INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION (web search of aviewfrommyseat.com 'is near the bullpen at Chase Field' tag page and andrewclem.com/Baseball/ChaseField.html): 'Diamondbacks Bullpen: The Diamondbacks bullpen is located in left field near Section 139. Visitors Bullpen: The visiting team's bullpen is located in right field near Section 105.' plus the geometric detail 'The bullpen on the right side (for the visiting team) is a few feet narrower than the home bullpen, which is why the right field line distance is five feet more than the left field line distance' - which reconciles with Wikipedia's asymmetric field dimensions 'Left Field - 330 ft ... Right Field - 334 ft'. NOTE the pleasing consistency: the Diamondbacks' bullpen (left field, 139) is on the same side of the park as the Diamondbacks' dugout (third base, N-Q), and the visiting bullpen (right field, 105) is on the same side as the visiting dugout (first base, C-F). That symmetry is itself a check that the dugout assignment above is not inverted. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the bullpens are at field level behind the fence or raised, and the exact sections they sit under beyond 105 and 139 - UNKNOWN.

accessibility.summary: Chase Field's accessible seating is integrated on every level and in every price range, including the Dugout Box. OFFICIAL, verbatim from the Diamondbacks Access Guide for Guests with Disabilities: 'Opening in 1998, Chase Field's accessible seating is integrated throughout the ballpark, meeting and exceeding the requirements for wheelchair locations and companion seats. These seating sections feature maximum flexibility by using removable tandems of stadium chairs that can be operated by any Guest Services Representative (the usher stationed in your section). When needed, folding chairs will be provided for guests. All seating price ranges have accessible seating available, including the Dugout Box seating. There are also Limited Mobility seats available for guests who have difficulty with stairs but do not use a wheelchair or mobility device.' Line of sight: 'All accessible seating is either front row or provides line of sight to the playing field and scoreboard over standing patrons. Access to front row seating is via elevators and ramps with a travel distance comparable to other front row seating for ambulatory spectators.' Power: 'Upper concourse wheelchair sections have electrical outlets available for charging wheelchair batteries or operating necessary medical equipment.' Entrances: 'All Chase Field entrances are located on accessible routes and are on the main concourse level, with accessible turnstiles located at Gates A, C, E North, J, K and Level 3 of the Chase Field Garage (for Suites and 200 level tickets).' Drop-off: 'The designated drop-off point for all guests is located on the south side of Jefferson Street, just west of 7th Street. This is at the northeast corner of Chase Field near Gate K. The Drop Off is staffed and there are shaded benches available for guests who need to wait for a companion to pick them up.' Wheelchair escorts: 'For guests who may have difficulty walking to their seats, Guest Relations provides complimentary wheelchair escort assistance from gates or drop off areas to the seats. There is no need to pre-schedule this service.' Storage: 'Guests wishing to check in their own walkers, wheelchairs, scooters or other mobility aids during the game may do so at the Guest Relations Centers located across from Sections 128 on the main concourse and 322 on the upper concourse.' Companions: 'A minimum of one and maximum of three adjacent companion seat(s) may be purchased for each wheelchair accessible seat purchased.' Contacts: accessible-seating line 602.462.6607, TDD 602.462.4180, single-game tickets 602.514.8400, Disability Services Manager/ADA Coordinator 602-462-6163, VideoPhone for the Deaf 623-208-7722, TDD 602-462-3189, email sholmes@dbacks.com.

row_seat_conventions: ROWS ARE MOSTLY NUMBERED, but the field-level lettered sections use LETTERED rows. Confirmed per level: (a) FIELD LEVEL - Clubhouse Box seats in Sections G-M are 'limited to Rows A-F'; 1st/3rd Base Box Sections A, B, R, S have 'just 7 rows' each and RateYourSeats' own photo filenames for those sections show 'Section-A-Row-G', 'Section-B-Row-G' and 'Section-R-Row-G', so those sections use lettered rows too; Dugout Box Sections C-F and N-Q run 'from Row 6 to Row 18, with Row 6 closest to the dugout' (NUMBERED), and RYS photo filenames confirm 'Section-C-Row-18', 'Section-N-Row-18'; Sections G-M also have photos captioned 'Section-G-Row-M', 'Section-L-Row-M', so the Home Plate Box rows behind the A-F Clubhouse Box rows continue in letters at least as far as M. So the lettered field ring mixes lettered and numbered row schemes - see 'uncertain'. (b) 100 LEVEL - numbered. Infield sections start at Row 21 because Rows 1-20 belong to the Field Level in front: Sections 122 and 128 are 'Rows 21-39, 40C-40W'; the RYS review states 'The seating sections start at row 21 in the front and run through row 39 in the back' and 'Most 100 level sections along the third base line end at Row 40'. Bleacher/corner sections start lower and run longer: Section 101 = 'Rows 22-31', Sections 143 and 144 = 'Rows 11-39, 40C-40W'; 'Some sections can have up to 40 rows'. (c) 200 LEVEL - numbered, short: 'Most sections feature fewer than 12 rows and around 20 seats per row'; the 210A-210I home-plate sections have 'no more than 2 rows of seating in each' and Section 210E is labelled 'Rows 1C, 1, 1W'. (d) 300 LEVEL - numbered, long: Section 316 = 'Rows 1-3, 4C-4W, 8-32'; 'Sections here are among some of the largest with up to 40 rows of seating per section' (infield) / 'up to 32 numbered rows' (corner). ENTRANCE-ROW BEHAVIOUR VARIES BY LEVEL AND IS THE OPPOSITE OF ITSELF IN PLACES: 100 Level infield sections are entered at the BACK - Sections 122 and 128 both say 'An entrance to this section is located at Row 40W'; 100 Level bleacher/corner sections are entered in the MIDDLE - Section 101 'An entrance to this section is located at Row 31', Section 143 'at Row 31', Section 144 'at Row 18'; 300 Level sections are entered near the FRONT - Section 316 'An entrance to this section is located at Row 4W', and the zone pages say 'Entry tunnels are located near the bottom of the sections (at Row 4)' and 'entry tunnels located near the front at Row 4'; 200 Level Section 210E 'An entrance to this section is located at Row 1W'. ACCESSIBLE-ROW LABEL CONVENTION - ESTABLISHED AND EXPLICIT: accessible rows are the SAME row number with a 'C' or 'W' SUFFIX, and they bracket the wheelchair platform. Observed: '40C-40W' (Sections 122, 128, 143, 144), '4C-4W' (Section 316), '1C-1W' (Section 100W), '1C, 1, 1W' (Section 210E). Section 316's page states verbatim: 'There is wheelchair seating betweeen Rows 4W and 8' [sic]. Interpretation: W = the wheelchair row, C = the adjoining companion row - this reading is CONSISTENT with every observation but is an INFERENCE, no source spells out what C and W stand for. There is NO 'WC', 'WCH', 'VWC' or 'AC' label anywhere at Chase Field. SECTION-LEVEL SUFFIXES: whole sections also carry a 'W' suffix - 100W, 145W, 224W, 300W, 332W, AW, BW, RFW - which are the dedicated wheelchair sections at the ends/corners of each tier (100W and 300W are photographed showing Rows '1C-1W' and '4W'). Two sections carry an 'L' suffix - 214L and 215L - which RateYourSeats lists with no photo, no rows and no description; the most likely reading is 'Limited Mobility', since the official D-backs guide says 'There are also Limited Mobility seats available for guests who have difficulty with stairs but do not use a wheelchair or mobility device' - but that mapping is an INFERENCE, see 'uncertain'. COLD BEER & CHEESEBURGERS TERRACE uses a 'T' row prefix for table seating: 'Choose between traditional seats or table seating (rows labeled "T")'. SEAT NUMBERING: see seat1_side_verbatim - Seat 1 is on the RIGHT when facing the field, so seat numbers increase in the SAME rotational direction as section numbers (from the right-field/first-base side toward the left-field/third-base side).
seat1_side_verbatim: PRIMARY (the RateYourSeats 'Row Numbers' block, quoted EXACTLY as printed, including the site's duplicated word 'field'): "When looking towards the field/field/stage, lower number seats are on the right". This sentence appeared VERBATIM AND IDENTICALLY on every individual section page fetched, with no variation whatsoever: https://www.rateyourseats.com/chase-field/seating/sections/100W , /sections/101 , /sections/122 , /sections/128 , /sections/143 , /sections/144 , /sections/210E and /sections/316 . Those eight pages span the right-field bleachers (100W, 101), the left-field bleachers (143, 144), the 100 Level behind home plate (122), the 100 Level third base line (128), the 200 Club Level behind home plate (210E) and the 300 Level behind home plate (316) - i.e. all four tiers and both sides of the park - so the rule is park-wide. INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION FROM A DIFFERENT PAGE TYPE, DIFFERENT WORDING, SAME ANSWER - the RateYourSeats MVP Box zone page states verbatim: "For reference, Seat 1 is located on the right side of the section when facing the field." (https://www.rateyourseats.com/chase-field/seating/mvp-box , and the same sentence is repeated in the MVP Box review block served on https://www.rateyourseats.com/chase-field/seating/sections/316). NO CONTRADICTION was found in any source. NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED: the field-level lettered sections A-S were not fetched individually, so seat 1's side there rests on the park-wide pattern only. Sections 214L, 215L, 224W, AW, BW and RFW have NO row/seat text at all on RateYourSeats - UNKNOWN.
known_obstructions: PROTECTIVE NETTING - TWO ACCOUNTS, RECORD BOTH. (a) RateYourSeats fan feedback, repeated on both Section 122 and Section 128, verbatim: 'Front of sections 115-129 are behind the netting - There is some amount of netting or screening in front of sections 115-129. The height and coverage of netting or screening will vary by section.' (b) RateYourSeats Dugout Box zone page, verbatim: 'Protective Netting: All seats behind netting for added safety' - covering field-level Sections C-F and N-Q. (c) A web-search summary of MLB.com press releases and Arizona Sports reporting states that the Diamondbacks extended netting to the far end of each dugout for 2018 and then 'the following season, the D-backs extended the netting all the way to the bullpen/foul pole area. The Diamondbacks extended Chase Field's netting to each foul pole.' (sources: https://www.mlb.com/press-release/d-backs-to-extend-netting-at-chase-field-265625550 , https://arizonasports.com/story/2067614/diamondbacks-to-extend-chase-field-safety-netting-farther-in-2020/ , https://www.abc15.com/sports/diamondbacks-to-expand-netting-around-chase-field-next-season ). CONFLICT: (a) implies netting covers only 115-129 while (c) implies it now runs foul pole to foul pole, i.e. roughly 106-138 plus the whole lettered ring. The RYS fan-feedback range is user-generated and may predate the 2020 extension. No official 2026 Diamondbacks netting diagram was retrievable. RECOMMENDED: treat the netted band as AT LEAST 115-129 and lettered Sections C-Q, and flag anything beyond that as unconfirmed. LEFT FIELD FOUL POLE - a real, sourced obstruction, and it is on the HIGH-numbered side. 100 Level, verbatim: 'In the left field corner, Sections 136-138 offer an interesting option... However the foul pole can cause some viewing obstructions in many of the areas, so we recommend staying in the lower numbered seats of Section 136 or the higher numbered seats of Section 138 where the sight lines are more clear.' 200 Level, verbatim: 'some obstructions will be found in Sections 221-223 due to the left field foul pole.' VIEWING-ANGLE (not physical) LIMITATIONS: All-You-Can-Eat 221-223 - 'the left field corner angle makes it harder to follow action at home plate. Fans sitting here should expect to turn slightly to follow the game'; Cold Beer & Cheeseburgers Terrace - 'Located beyond the outfield wall, these seats are far from home plate and offer a more distant perspective of the game'; Dugout Box - 'Because the dugouts sit below field level, these seats are slightly elevated above the players' (so not obstructed by the dugout roof); Clubhouse Box / lettered sections for football - 'a very shallow seating height making it difficult to follow the action at the far endzone' and 'a poor viewing height for seeing all areas of the field'; 300 Level - 'the highest seating area at Chase Field, offering less desirable views of the field than most other areas at the ballpark' and Wikipedia's 'With 80% of the seats in foul territory, the upper deck is one of the highest in the majors.' VIDEOBOARD: the main board sits above the 25-foot centre-field batter's-eye wall and was replaced for 2026 with a 9,600 sq ft screen; RateYourSeats notes for football that 'left field seats will have a difficult head turn to see the videoboard'. NO pole or railing obstruction reports were found for the seating bowl itself. SUN (not an obstruction, and largely moot because the roof is usually closed): right field / first base side is the sunny side; sections 101-110 are 'particularly exposed'; the third base side is the shade side; 300 Level Sections 314-318 and 328-332 sit under permanent roof structures, and the back rows of 319-327 also get roof cover.
uncertain: VENUE NAME: no rename found and none announced - the Chase naming-rights deal runs '$2.2 million/year through 2028' per Ballparks of Baseball. But Arizona HB2704 (signed September 2025) funds a major Chase Field renovation, and renovations of this kind are a common trigger for renaming and for section renumbering. Re-verify the venue name AND the section map before each future season.

ORIENTATION PRECISION: ShadedSeats says 'Chase Field is oriented to the north'; a second source says the stadium 'faces northeast'. No source gives degrees. The sun path (rises over the right field corner, sets behind the left field wall) and the official statement that Gate K / Section 105 is at the ballpark's NORTHEAST corner both support 'centre field roughly north, right field roughly east', but treat the exact bearing as low confidence. Also note orientation barely matters here because the roof is usually closed.

CAPACITY: 48,330 (Wikipedia 'since 2023', and Itinerant Fan March 2026) vs 48,633 (Ballparks of Baseball, which is Wikipedia's 2011-2014 figure). Recommended 48,330. Wikipedia's figure has changed nine times since 1998, so re-check annually.

100 LEVEL HOME-PLATE CENTRE: only Section 122 is explicitly flagged 'Home Plate View' / 'desirable view from behind home plate'. The surrounding behind-the-plate arc (roughly 118-127) is an INFERENCE from the netting range 115-129 and the flanking elevators at 117 and 127. Do not publish 121 or 123 as 'behind home plate' without a source.

300 LEVEL HOME-PLATE CENTRE: only Section 316 is explicitly flagged. ShadedSeats' 'directly behind home plate' band is 314-318 and the flanking elevators are 310 and 321, so 315/316 is the centre, but 315 is not individually sourced.
FIELD-LEVEL LETTER CENTRE: no source names a single letter as dead centre behind the plate. G-M is the sourced block; J is the arithmetic middle but that is an INFERENCE.

FIELD-LEVEL ROW SCHEME IS MIXED AND ONLY PARTLY SOURCED: Clubhouse Box G-M is stated to be 'Rows A-F'; Dugout Box C-F and N-Q is stated to be 'Rows 6 to 18'. But RateYourSeats photo filenames show 'Section-A-Row-G', 'Section-B-Row-G', 'Section-R-Row-G' and 'Section-G-Row-M', 'Section-L-Row-M' - implying the 1st/3rd Base Boxes and the Home Plate Box also use lettered rows running past F. The full row list for any lettered section was NOT retrieved (those section pages were not fetched individually). How lettered rows and numbered rows coexist within a single lettered section is UNKNOWN.

'L' SUFFIX SECTIONS 214L AND 215L: RateYourSeats lists them in the index with no photo, no rows, no zone and no description; the page body is empty apart from a price. The official D-backs guide mentions 'Limited Mobility seats... for guests who have difficulty with stairs but do not use a wheelchair', which makes 'L = Limited Mobility' the most plausible reading, but NOTHING states this. Treat as UNKNOWN.

'W' SUFFIX SECTIONS: 100W, 145W, 224W, 300W, 332W, AW, BW and RFW are almost certainly wheelchair sections (100W and 300W are photographed and use rows '1C-1W' / '4W'), but 145W, 224W, 332W, AW, BW and RFW have NO RateYourSeats content at all - no rows, no photo, no description. 'RFW' presumably means 'Right Field Wheelchair' but that is an INFERENCE; note it is grouped alphabetically with the lettered field sections in the RYS index, between R and S.

'C' AND 'W' ROW SUFFIXES: the reading 'W = wheelchair row, C = companion row' fits every observation (1C/1W, 4C/4W, 40C/40W, and '1C, 1, 1W' on 210E) and fits Section 316's 'There is wheelchair seating betweeen Rows 4W and 8', but no source defines the letters. Publish the labels, not the expansion.

NETTING EXTENT: RateYourSeats fan feedback says 115-129; 2019/2020 news reporting says the netting was extended 'all the way to the bullpen/foul pole area' and 'to each foul pole'. These are irreconcilable from the sources available, and no official 2026 Diamondbacks netting map was retrievable. The fan feedback may simply be stale.

OFFICIAL RAMP LIST CONTRADICTS ITSELF: the Diamondbacks ADA page gives ramp locations twice - once as 'Main Level-Across from Section 111 / Upper Level-Across from Section 301' and once as 'Main Level-Across from Section 110 / Upper Level-Across from Section 301'. Both are on the same official page. Record both; do not pick silently.

WEB-SEARCH ELEVATOR NUMBERS WERE WRONG: a search summary of the same official ADA page reported elevators 'across from sections 104 and 300', 'across from sections 116, 208, and 309' and 'across from sections 140, 223, and 332'. The directly fetched page says 105/200/300, 117/209/310, 127/211/321 and 139/223/332. This is a live example of a secondary summary corrupting a symmetric landmark - always prefer the fetched page.

200 LEVEL CLUB RANGE VS INDEX: RateYourSeats says the Club Level 'includes sections 200-220', yet 221, 222 and 223 exist in the index (All-You-Can-Eat, left field corner) and 224W exists with no description. Whether 221-224W are formally part of the Club/Diamond Level is not stated.

SECTION INDEX COMPLETENESS: the RYS index is used verbatim above (138 baseball section identifiers). It contains no gaps in the 101-144 or 301-332 runs, which is reassuring, but it has not been reconciled against the official Diamondbacks seating chart (https://www.ballparksofbaseball.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/chase_seating_chart.jpg was identified but not fetched). Suite and party-suite identifiers (57 suites, 6 party suites, Executive suite, batter's box suite, two Dugout Suites, the Pool Suite per Wikipedia) are NOT in the RYS index and are UNKNOWN.

CONCERT FLOOR: RYS lists 'Field 1' through 'Field 9' at URLs /sections/1 .. /sections/9 with no photos and no descriptions; the zone page describes an outfield stage and a possible GA pit but does not enumerate the labels. Whether the ticketed labels really read 'Field 1' or something else is UNKNOWN. Excluded from baseball sections.
COLD BEER & CHEESEBURGERS TERRACE has no numbered section identifiers on RateYourSeats at all - only the zone and the 'T' table-row convention. Its actual ticketed section IDs are UNKNOWN.

BULLPEN GEOMETRY: sourced only to 'near Section 105' (visitors, right field) and 'near Section 139' (Diamondbacks, left field). Whether they are at field level behind the fence, stacked, or angled is not stated.

HOME DUGOUT IS ON THE THIRD BASE SIDE - this is the minority arrangement in MLB and is the single most likely thing for a downstream guide to invert. It is confirmed by two independent sources (RateYourSeats Dugout Box page and Ballparks of Baseball '-Home Dugout: Third Base') and is corroborated by the bullpen sides (D-backs bullpen in left field, same side as the D-backs dugout). Do not 'correct' it.

PAGE FETCH NOTES: https://www.mlb.com/dbacks/ballpark/accessibility returned an EMPTY body; https://www.rateyourseats.com/chase-field (bare slug) returned an EMPTY body - use https://www.rateyourseats.com/venues/chase-field or /chase-field/seating instead. The official ADA page exceeded the fetch size limit and had to be read from a saved file; it was read in full for the sections quoted above but the omitted long lines (parking detail, alternative-format materials, ticketing policy preamble) were only partially reviewed.
